title: FloodPay Term Length, Renewal Notice and Return-Premium Settings
content:
This servicing schedule records, for each tier of FloodPay Parametric Flood Cover (Surplus Lines), the length of a term, the timing of renewal offers and of a Tidemark non-renewal notice, and the settings that govern how premium is returned when a policyholder cancels.

| Tier | Term length (calendar months) | Renewal offer issued before term end (calendar days) | Written notice before term end for a Tidemark non-renewal (calendar days) | Credit method on a policyholder cancellation | Share of the term premium fully earned at activation (%) | Term premium fully earned once a payout has been made |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FloodPay Home 5K | 12 | 45 | 45 | Pro rata | 25 | Yes |
| FloodPay Home 10K | 12 | 45 | 45 | Pro rata | 25 | Yes |
| FloodPay Home 25K | 12 | 45 | 45 | Pro rata | 25 | Yes |
| FloodPay Business 50K | 12 | 45 | 45 | Pro rata | 25 | Yes |
| FloodPay Business 100K | 12 | 45 | 45 | Pro rata | 25 | Yes |
| FloodPay Business 250K | 12 | 45 | 45 | Pro rata | 25 | Yes |

## The schedule in words

- **Term length.** A FloodPay term runs 12 calendar months on every tier.
- **Renewal offer.** The renewal offer is issued 45 calendar days before term end.
- **Non-renewal notice.** A Tidemark non-renewal requires written notice 45 calendar days before term end.
- **Credit method.** A policyholder cancellation is credited pro rata.
- **Minimum earned share.** 25 percent of the term premium is fully earned at activation.
- **Earned after payout.** On every tier the term premium is fully earned once a payout has been made.

## Basis Q&A

**Does any of these settings differ between the Home and Business tiers?**
No. The figures and settings in this schedule are the same on all six FloodPay tiers.

**What does the 25 percent figure represent?**
It is the share of the term premium that is fully earned at activation; it is stated as a percent of the term premium.
